text:
alex: Heads-up — saw a cluster-wide latency spike in eu-west around 07:12. Correlates with GPU memory pressure on shared pools (rack-eu-3). infra-bot posted an alert.
infra-bot: [ALERT] gpu_mem_pressure HIGH on rack-eu-3 · affected_slots=18 · avg_gpu_free=1.6GB · time=2024-11-21T07:12:14Z
maya: Ugh. That rack is 50% shared-slice. Might be mixed-precision jobs ballooning KV caches. Any OOM counts?
alex: Early numbers: ~12 allocation OOMs across tenants, 6 preemptive evictions, and a handful of retries causing request latency to spike to 800ms p50 for text-gen routes.
igor: Do we have a quick query to surface top tenants by transient GPU memory usage? I can run it.
alex: Use this metric query in telemetry: `topk(5, increase(gpu_mem_alloc_bytes[10m])) by (tenant)` — returns tenant IDs and bytes. Also check `gpu_kv_cache_size_bytes` per tenant.
samir: If KV caches are unbounded under shared slices that explains cascading evictions. Proposed mitigation: introduce a soft cap per-tenant KV cache + LRU eviction stepdown when cluster_free < 3GB per GPU. That would avoid OOM spikes but might regress token latency slightly.
maya: Soft caps sound reasonable. What's the operational cost vs. creating more dedicated 'warm' slices? Cold dedicated pools cost more but avoid multi-tenant interference.
igor: Quick math: the eu-west shared pool is saving ~28% on infra cost vs. dedicated slice pricing historically. If we shift 8 high-memory tenants to dedicated, infra cost delta ~+12% but 99.9 latency SLO would improve.
linh: We should also consider routing rules: route heavy KV-cache-heavy sessions to pre-warmed pinned GPUs (cheaper than full dedicated) — i.e., short-lived pinned lanes. That reduces cost vs full dedicated and gives isolation.
alex: Implementation plan suggestion:
1) Roll a soft cap feature flag for KV cache at tenant level (default off) and enable for top-5 offenders in canary region (eu-west-rack3).
2) Add autoscaler hook: if cluster_free_per_gpu < 3GB, clamp KV cache to 512MB per tenant in shared pools.
3) Add a routing policy to prefer pinned lanes for tenants with sustained KV > 1GB for > 10m.
4) Telemetry dashboards + regression alert for token latency and generation errors.
maya: +1. Need a quick experiment to validate latency tradeoffs. Can someone ship a canary by EOD?
samir: I can do the canary for step (1) and (2). Will gate behind feature flag `kv_softcap/v1`. Rolling to 10% of shared pool tomorrow morning.
igor: I'll prepare the telemetry query and a quick grafana panel. Also add a synthetic load that reproduces the mix-precision KV growth so we can run the canary under load.
linh: I'll update routing rules with a canary config: `route.prefer_pinned = tenant.kv_cache > 1GB && tenant.sla == "gold"`. We'll simulate with a non-prod tenant first.
alex: FYI: we've seen one tenant repeatedly causing spikes — tenant-42. Samir, include them in the canary target list and notify their owner (cc @oncall).
maya: Also PID: we should estimate cost delta if canary shows 20% latency hit. If unacceptable, escalate to dedicated conversion.
samir: Noted. I'll post preliminary numbers in this thread after the canary run (expected tomorrow +3h). For now, enabling the soft cap is low-risk and reversible.
igor: Small note: ensure the eviction backoff doesn't create a thundering retry storm — add randomized jitter to cache trim and a per-tenant cooldown.
alex: Good call. Add 30-120s jitter and exponential backoff on retries.
linh: I'll draft a short runbook for SRE response if the canary causes regressions. Also will add a log marker when we clamp caches so we can filter incidents.
maya: Thanks — once canary completes, let's reconvene and decide whether to move tenants to pinned lanes or dedicated based on cost + SLOs.
alex: 👍 will create follow-up ticket and link telemetry. Thanks everyone.
